content.prompt: What happens to each function as $t\to\infty$?

answer.worked: As $t\to\infty$, $-t\to-\infty$, so $e^{-t}\to0$. The exponential decays faster than $5t$ grows, so $y\to0$.
As $t\to\infty$, $t-0.2t^2\to-\infty$, so $e^{t-0.2t^2}\to0$. The exponential decays faster than $t^2+1$ grows, so $y\to0$.

payloads.replacement: Change the base of an exponential using $e^{\log_e a}=a$, where $a>0$.

Every positive real number $a$ can be written with base $e$: $a=e^{\ln a}$

For $a>0$, every exponential function $a^x$ can be written with base $e$: $a^x=e^{x\ln a}$

To differentiate an exponential function with any base $a>0$:

$f(x)$	$=$	$a^x$
$f'(x)$	$=$	$(\ln a)\,a^x$
